rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لئن prepares the oath’s answer; calling it preparatory to the oath itself is loose usage.
rows.anchor: وقول المعربين إنها موطئة للقسم فيه تجوز وإنما هي موطئة لجوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse the lām in لئن signals an implied oath, while لنسفعا is its answer: By God, We will seize him.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم المقدر تقديره والله لنسفعن

rows.speaker: أثيرالدين
rows.claim: Athir al-Din calls the lām an emphatic lām, but al-Zarkashi rejects that analysis.
rows.anchor: زعم الشيخ أثيرالدين في تفسيره أنها لام التوكيد وليس كما قال

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi calls it the lām of an oath; an initial lām cannot attach to anything but a noun or noun-like form.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الواحدي في البسيط إنها لام القسم ولا يجوز أن تكون لام ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second class of lām is governing, and it has three forms: prepositional, subjunctive, and jussive.
rows.anchor: وهي على ثلاثة أقسام جارة وناصبة وجازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional lām can denote actual ownership, as in the earth, the heavens, and God’s armies belonging to Him.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mark transfer of ownership, as when someone gives a dinar to Zayd or God grants mercy to others.
rows.anchor: والتمليك نحو وهبت لزيد دينارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can express a relation or association between two things, as in calling someone Zayd’s friend or brother.
rows.anchor: والاختصاص ومعناها أنها تدل على إن بين الأول والثاني نسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām also marks specification, as in a woman offering herself specifically to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وللتخصيص ومنه ﴿ إن وهبت نفسها للنبي ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mark entitlement, as in woe belonging to the defrauders and the curse and evil abode belonging to others.
rows.anchor: لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes entitlement from ownership: ownership is already established, while entitlement is future but treated as established.
rows.anchor: الفرق بينه وبين الملك أن الملك لما حصل وثبت وهذا لم يحصل بعد لكن هو في حكم الحاصل من حيث ما قد استحق قاله الراغب

words: لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may also signify guardianship or authority, as in God’s command belonging to Him before and after.
rows.anchor: وللولاية كقوله ﴿ لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three senses can coincide in praise of God: He deserves praise, has authority over it, and is the one to whom it belongs.
rows.anchor: ويجوز إن تجمع هذه الثلاثة كقولك الحمد لله لأنه يستحق الحمد ووليه والمخصوص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions of the announced boys as forbearing and learned characterize them by the qualities they would later attain.
rows.anchor: وصفة في حال البشارة بما يئول اليه من العلم والحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prospective circumstantial phrase conveys an intended or anticipated state, rather than a completed state already accompanying the subject or object.
rows.anchor: ليس هذا من الحال المقدرة كما يتبادر إلى الذهن لان الذي يقترن بالفاعل أو المفعول انما هو تقدير ذلك وارادته

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali takes the falling in prostration as its beginning, which makes the accompanying state prospective; taking it as completed makes the state actual.
rows.anchor: على قول أبي علي وهذا حمل منه للخرور على ابتدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering Paradise while anticipating permanent residence completes the joy; imagining a later departure would spoil the present delight.
rows.anchor: اي ادخلوها مقدرين الخلود فيها فان من دخل مدخلا كريما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling heirs orphans can name them by their former status, since orphanhood ends at puberty.
rows.anchor: أي الذين كانوا يتامى اذ لايتم بعد البلوغ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the people addressed as genuine orphans.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل هم يتامى حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying that there is no orphanhood after puberty is a teaching of religious law, not a linguistic rule; al-Zarkashi calls this unusual.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث لايتم بعد احتلام فهو من تعليم الشرع لا اللغة وهو غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wives are still called wives in inheritance wording after death has ended the marriage, because they were once spouses.
rows.anchor: وإذا متن لم يكن أزواجا فسماهن بذلك لانهن كن أزواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Former husbands can still be called the women’s husbands when the text speaks of their marrying them again.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن ﴾ أي الذين كانوا أزواجهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Widows are called wives even though their husbands’ deaths ended the marriage.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ﴿ ويذرون أزواجا ﴾ لانقطاع الزوجية بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who comes to his Lord as a criminal is named by the criminal state he had in worldly life.
rows.anchor: سماه مجرما باعتبار ما كان عليه في الدنيا من الاجرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brothers call the returned goods theirs because they had once owned them, although they had exchanged them for provisions and Joseph had placed them in their baggage.
rows.anchor: ولكن ما رد عليهم مالهم وإنما كانوا قد اشتروا بها الميرة فجعلها يوسف في متاعهم وهي له دونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place name in ناديه stands for the people who gather there: this is naming the occupant by the location.
rows.anchor: السادس عشر إطلاق اسم المحل على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised couches refer to their women, as shown by the following statement that God created them anew.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وفرش مرفوعة ﴾ اي نساؤه بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hand is used figuratively for power in the expression that sovereignty is in His hand.
rows.anchor: وكالتعبير باليد عن القدرة كقوله

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Abd al-Aziz treats ويمح الله الباطل as a new sentence, not the conditional answer, because erasing falsehood is already established.
rows.anchor: وهذا ملخص كلام عبد العزيز في كلامه على البزدوي وفيما ذكره نزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi disputes that the conditional content is already true before its condition: here the condition is God’s willing, and erasure is not established before that will.
rows.anchor: لانسلم أن المعلق ها هنا بالشرط هو موجود قبل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the omitted condition is specifically willing to seal the heart, its object is understood from context; examples show such ellipsis, and erasure precedes that particular will.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل إن الشرط هنا مشيئة خاصة وهي مشيئة الختم وهذا وإن كان محذوفا فهو مذكور بالقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the answer specifies both sealing and erasure, a condition must be neither already established nor impossible; erasure was already established, so it cannot be in the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: ويمحو الباطل كان ثابتا فلا يصح دخوله في جواب الشرط وهذا أحسن جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted final waw in the pause forms is explained by pausing; Yaqub’s pause with the waw confirms this.
rows.anchor: فللوقف ويؤكد ذلك وقوف يعقوب عليها بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reordered phrase means abstain from idols, which are a kind of impurity.
rows.anchor: الأوثان ﴾ 6 أي الاوثان من الرجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that they fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: لربهم يرهبون ﴾ 7 أي يرهبون ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means people who preserve their private parts.
rows.anchor: لفروجهم حافظون ﴾ 8 أي الذين هم حافظون لفروجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reordered wording means that God will not fail His messengers in His promise to them.
rows.anchor: مخلف وعده رسله ﴾ 9 أي مخلف رسله وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a person sees or bears witness against himself, with his limbs testifying against him.
rows.anchor: على نفسه بصيرة ﴾ 10 أي بل الإنسان بصير على نفسه في شهود جوارحه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that haste was created in the human being.
rows.anchor: ﴿ خلق الإنسان من عجل ﴾ 11 خلق العجل من الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that without a prior decree and appointed term from God, punishment would have become binding on them.
rows.anchor: أي ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك وأجل مسمى لكان العذاب لازما لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks how your Lord extended the shade.
rows.anchor: كيف مد الظل ﴾ 1 أي كيف مده ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reordered phrase means that he is intense in his love of wealth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ﴾ 2 أي لشديد لحب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the partners of many polytheists made killing their children seem fair; devils urged killing daughters from fear of dishonor.
rows.anchor: قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ﴾ 3 أي زين للمشركين شركاؤهم قتل أولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also lists the phrase about those who infer the matter as an example in this reordered-expression discussion.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ﴾ 4

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also lists the phrase about God’s favor and mercy among these reordered expressions.
rows.anchor: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not be impressed by their worldly wealth and children: God intends to punish them through these things in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم في الحياة الدنيا إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The structure means that the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ash scattered by the wind.
rows.anchor: تقديره مثل الذين كفروا بربهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says he is an enemy of their idols and every object of worship besides the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: أي فأنا عدو آلهتهم وأصنامهم وكل معبود يعبدونه من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event order is that they were frightened and seized, after which there was no escape, since escape follows seizure.
rows.anchor: أي فزعوا وأخذوا فلا فوت لأن الفوت يكون بعد الأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces toil in worldly life and are downcast on Resurrection Day; the order is reversed, as the later description of joyful faces confirms.
rows.anchor: والنصب والعمل يكونان في الدنيا فكأنه على التقديم والتأخير معناه وجوه عاملة ناصبة

rows.speaker: ابن خروف
rows.claim: Ibn Khuruf says jurists use arāʾayta with an implicit hypothetical condition, followed by a question whose clause is suspended from governing action, like the Quranic pattern.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خروف إلا أنهم يلجئون فيها وجوابها أرايت إن كان كذا وكذا كيف يكون كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل, the verb carries wonder, roughly meaning do you not marvel; its action is suspended by the interrogative clause, not replaced by the Lord.
rows.anchor: دخلها معنى التعجب كأنه قيل ألم تعجب إلى كذا فتعدت ب إلى كأنه ألم تنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form arāʾaytaka is unusual because it combines the tāʾ of the verb with a kāf of address; the doubled address highlights its threatening context.
rows.anchor: جمع فيها بين علامتي خطاب وهما التاء والكاف والتاء اسم بخلاف الكاف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the extra address particle stresses deep heedlessness, like waking someone by touch; Yunus omits it because preceding questions had already roused the audience.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر بن الزبير الاتيان باداة الخطاب بعد الضمير المفيد لذلك تاكيد باستحكام غفلته كما تحرك النائم باليد

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrians treat kāf as an extra particle of address; Muhammad ibn Yazid supports this because أرأيتك زيدا means أرأيت زيدا, while a noun kāf would make the object syntax impossible.
rows.anchor: قال البصريون ( 4 ) هذه الكاف زائدة زيدت لمعنى المخاطبة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash permits omitting the fāʾ where Sibawayh requires it and cites وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون as evidence.
rows.anchor: جوز حذف الفاء حيث يوجب سيبويه دخولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first citation does not prove omission: its second clause can answer an implicit oath, while the oath answer replaces the missing conditional result.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة فيه لأن الأول يجوز إن يكون جواب قسم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash also cites a reading attributed to Nafi and Ibn Amir concerning the fāʾ after ما أصابكم من مصيبة.
rows.anchor: في قراءة نافع وابن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That reading is no evidence for fāʾ after a conditional, since ما here is a relative pronoun, not a conditional particle.
rows.anchor: وأما الثانية فلأن ما فيه موصولة لا شرطية فلم يجز دخول الفاء في خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this example the fāʾ is treated as extra; حميم is the predicate, with the intervening material parenthetical.
rows.anchor: والرابع الزائدة كقوله تعالى ﴿ فليذوقوه حميم ﴾ 4

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the fāʾ in فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم as an extra particle.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه الأخفش ﴿ فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh instead analyzes the fāʾ as the result of an omitted condition: if you wanted to rebuke him, then this is the one.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه هي جواب لشرط مقدر أي إن أردت عليه فذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in فصل لربك وانحر is also counted as extra according to one reported view.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فصل لربك وانحر ﴾ 6 على قول

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Surat al-Maun is Meccan except from فويل للمصلين through its end, which is Medinan.
rows.anchor: سورة ﴿ أرأيت ﴾ مكية إلا قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ إلى آخرها فإنها مدنية كذا قال مقاتل بن سليمان

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم بن جبيب النيسابورى
rows.claim: Ibn Habib, al-Baghawi, al-Kawashi, and others define interpretive inference as a linguistically possible meaning consistent with surrounding verses and not contrary to Qur'an or Sunnah.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو القاسم بن جبيب النيسابورى والبغوى والكواشى وغيرهم التأويل صرف الآية إلى معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These scholars say such inference is permitted to qualified exegetes and the scholarly permission is established.
rows.anchor: قالوا وهذا غير محظور على العلماء بالتفسير وقد رخص فيه أهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of ruin is a fighter charging a force of a hundred in battle.
rows.anchor: قيل هو الرجل يحمل في الحرب على مائة رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of ruin is despairing of God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الذي يقنط من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is withholding expenditure.
rows.anchor: وقيل الذي يمسك عن النفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is spending the bad part of one’s wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الذي ينفق الخبيث من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is giving away all one’s wealth and then begging people.
rows.anchor: وقيل الذي يتصدق بماله كله ثم يتكفف الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of light and heavy is young and old.
rows.anchor: قيل شيوخا وشبابا وقيل أغنياء وفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is rich and poor.
rows.anchor: قيل أغنياء وفقراء وقيل عزابا ومتأهلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is single and married.
rows.anchor: قيل عزابا ومتأهلين وقيل نشاطا وغير نشاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is energetic and unenergetic.
rows.anchor: قيل نشاطا وغير نشاط وقيل مرضى وأصحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is sick and healthy.
rows.anchor: قيل مرضى وأصحاء وكلها سائغ جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these readings are acceptable because the young, single, energetic, and healthy are light, while their opposites are heavy.
rows.anchor: وكلها سائغ جائز والآية محمولة عليها لان الشباب والعزاب والنشاط والأصحاء خفاف وضدهم ثقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of al-maun is the obligatory alms tax.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويمنعون الماعون ﴾ قيل الزكاة المفروضة وقيل العارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is a loaned or borrowed item.
rows.anchor: قيل العارية أو الماء أو النار أو الكلأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is water.
rows.anchor: العارية أو الماء أو النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is fire.
rows.anchor: الماء أو النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is pasture or grazing land.
rows.anchor: النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is assistance or support.
rows.anchor: الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is a ladle.
rows.anchor: أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every cited meaning is valid, since withholding each of these items is sinful.
rows.anchor: وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd explains worshipping God on an edge as not persisting in faith.
rows.anchor: فسره أبو عبيد أي لايدوم وقال ثعلب أي على شك

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab explains worshipping God on an edge as worshipping while in doubt.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب أي على شك وكلاهما قريب لأن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings are close: the person is unstable in religion and lacks settled insight.
rows.anchor: وكلاهما قريب لأن المراد انه غير ثابت على دينة ولا تستقيم البصيرة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported saying identifies three Quranic verses with a hundred interpretations each: remember Me, if you return We return, and is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?
rows.anchor: وقيل في القرآن ثلاث آيات في كل منها مائة قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deriving such meanings is not forbidden but necessary knowledge; God would not mention seeking its interpretation if no linguistically sound interpretation existed.
rows.anchor: فهذا وأمثاله ليس محظورا على العلماء استخراجه بل معرفة واجبة

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو المعالي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu al-Maali says stopping after والراسخون is the majority view and the position of Ibn Masud, Ubayy ibn Kab, and Ibn Abbas; contrary reports are mistaken.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو المعالي انه قول الجمهور وهو مذهب ابن مسعود وابي بن كعب وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three surahs open with an invocation or curse: al-Mutaffifin, al-Humaza, and al-Masad.
rows.anchor: التاسع الدعاء فى ثلاث سور ﴿ ويل للمطففين ﴾ ﴿ ويل لكل همزة ﴾ ﴿ تبت يدا أبي لهب ﴾

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashari, Qadi Abu Bakr, Ibn Hibban, and others deny that one passage is better than another: all is God’s speech, and calling one best implies deficiency in another.
rows.anchor: ذهب الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعرى والقاضى أبو بكر وأبو حاتم بن حبان وغيرهم إلى أنه لا فضل لبعض على بعض

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik’s view is reported as denying preference; Yahya ibn Yahya calls it wrong to prefer one part, and Malik disliked repeatedly reciting one surah over others.
rows.anchor: وروي معناه عن مالك قال يحيى بن يحيى تفضيل بعض القرآن على بعض خطأ وكذلك كره مالك أن تعاد سورة

rows.speaker: ابن حبان
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban reads the report comparing al-Fatiha with the Torah and Gospel as a difference in reward granted by God’s favor, not as intrinsic superiority within the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حبان فى حديث أبى بن كعب رضى الله عنه ما أنزل الله فى التوارة ولا فى الإنجيل مثل أم القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن حبان
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban says calling al-Fatiha the greatest surah means greatest in reward, not that one part of the Quran is intrinsically superior.
rows.anchor: قال وقوله أعظم سورة أراد به فى الأجر لا أن بعض القرآن أفضل من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some proponents explain preference through greater reward, varying with spiritual response, reverence, reflection, and contemplation of exalted descriptions.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم الفضل راجع إلى عظم الأجر ومضاعفة الثواب بحسب انفعالات النفس وخشيتها وتدبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi prefers that preference rests on the abundance and wonder of meanings: divine unity and attributes occur in these passages but not in the curse on Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: فالتفضيل إنما هو بالمعاني العجيبة وكثرتها لا من حيث الصفة وهذا هو الحق

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
rows.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and other scholars are among those who affirm that some parts of the Quran are preferable to others.
rows.anchor: وممن قال بالتفضيل إسحاق بن راهويه وغيره من العلماء

rows.speaker: عز الدين
rows.claim: Izz al-Din takes a middle position: speech about God is better than speech about others, so al-Ikhlas is better than the surah about Abu Lahab; al-Ghazali and Ibn al-Arabi adopted this.
rows.anchor: وتوسط الشيخ عز الدين فقال كلام الله فى الله أفضل من كلام الله فى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Said reports the Prophet calling al-Fatiha the greatest surah in a Bukhari narration; al-Zarkashi says this does not conflict with Ayat al-Kursi’s rank among verses, since the comparisons concern surahs and verses respectively.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يعارض ما قبله بأفضلية الفاتحة لأن تلك باعتبار السور وهذه باعتبار الآيات

words: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم
rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In the two Sahih collections, the Prophet asks Ubayy for the greatest verse; Ubayy names Ayat al-Kursi, and the Prophet praises his knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولحديث أبى بن كعب فى الصحيحين قال لى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أى آية فى كتاب الله أعظم

words: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Hakim reports with a sound chain from Abu Hurayra that Ayat al-Kursi is the foremost verse of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم فى مستدركه بسند صحيح عن أبى هريرة سيدة آي القرآن آية الكرسى

words: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports a rare raised narration from Abu Hurayra that every thing has a peak and the Quran’s peak is al-Baqara, which contains Ayat al-Kursi.
rows.anchor: وفى الترمذى غريبا عنه مرفوعا لكل شىء سنام وإن سنام القرآن سورة البقرة فيها آية الكرسى

words: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم
rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna transmits from Abu Salih that Ayat al-Kursi is the peak of Quranic verses and that reciting it in a house expels Satan.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عيينة فى جامعه عن أبى صالح عنه فيها آية الكرسى وهى سنام آى القرآن ولا تقرأ فى دار فيها شيطان

rows.speaker: القاضي شمس الدين الخويي
rows.claim: Al-Khuyi says eloquence comparisons must respect each passage’s purpose: no wording better invokes ruin than Tabbat, and no wording better states divine unity than al-Ikhlas, so neither is absolutely more eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضى شمس الدين الخويى كلام الله أبلغ من كلام المخلوقين وهل يجوز أن يقال بعض كلامه أبلغ من بعض

rows.speaker: القاضي شمس الدين الخويي
rows.claim: Comparing al-Ikhlas directly with Tabbat is misguided if it pits divine mention against Abu Lahab or monotheism against a curse; each is most eloquent in its own subject.
rows.anchor: يجعل المقابلة بين ذكر الله وذكر أبي لهب وبين التوحيد والدعاء على الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi suggests this disagreement may track the broader Ashari debate over whether God’s speech is one in itself or varies according to its objects.
rows.anchor: ولعل الخلاف فى هذه المسألة يلفت عن الخلاف المشهور إن كلام الله شىء واحد أولا عند الأشعرى أنه لا يتنوع فى ذاته
